description: Synthetic messages for deterministic safety-routing regression. All text is invented; no real student data. expected_lane is the safety router lane the DISPATCHER must honour (null = no lane). This is a regression suite written alongside the rules, so recall measured on it is optimistic; an independent held-out set is still required (see docs/safety/crisis-routing.md).

kinds.positive: plain wording that must reach the lane
kinds.adversarial: obfuscated wording (spacing, leetspeak, homoglyphs, invisible characters)
kinds.multi_intent: message mixing a safety signal with a decline or FAQ intent; tests precedence
kinds.negation: negated crisis wording; routed to crisis on purpose (fail-safe policy)
kinds.negative: benign wording that must NOT reach a safety-critical lane (false-positive guard)
kinds.non_critical: must reach a specific non-safety-critical lane (retention, counseling) and get its template, never generic alternatives or a wrong lane
